newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian stock markets cautious after sharp rally on Wednesday, fund managers sceptical

** World oil prices extended losses on Wednesday following news that Iraq was coming back and also, of more immediate impact, data showing that depleted U.S. heating fuel stocks are at last starting to fill up
Benchmark Brent Blend crude from the North Sea for January delivery traded as low as $22.40 a barrel, down from Tuesday's close at $23.29
** India may need to import one million tonnes of wheat in the coming months, U.S. Wheat Associates says
** France's Credit Commercial de France said on Wednesday it bought five percent of the capital of the Indian company Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services Ltd (IL&FS)
IL&FS was created in 1988 by three of India's biggest financial institutions -- Central Bank of India, Unit Trust of India and Housing Development Finance Corporation Ltd
** Qatar in deal with India's Essar Oil Ltd to sell 2.5 million tonnes of liquified natural gas (LNG)-official
It also in talks with state-run Gas Authority of India Ltd to sell another 2 to 2.5 million tonnes of LNG
** Canada's Dominion Textile Inc said on Wednesday that it agreed with LNJ Bhilwara Group to cancel their proposed joint venture project to build a denim manufacturing facility in India due to delays
** India's Dabur group entered into a tie-up with Liberty International Holding Inc of the U.S. to set up a joint venture in the general insurance sector-company official
** Clearance for state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd's expansion plan to be on priority basis-ministry

The firm plans to expand smelter and refining capacity at its Khetri complex in northern Rajasthan state to 100,000 tonnes per annum of copper from 31,000 tonnes at a cost of nearly 5.3 billion rupees
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.83/85 per dollar and seen steady, dealers say
MARKETS:
** Indian share prices reversed a three-week slide and rebounded sharply on Wednesday, bolstered by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Dowda's promise to review a minimum tax on firms-brokers
** The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange .BSESN leapt 142.79 points, or 5.10 percent, to close at 2,941.36
** The 50 stock National Stock Exchange index rose 33.87 points to 838.07.
** New York stocks, bonds and the dollar all tumbled Wednesday on renewed fears of an interest rate hike and fresh worries about corporate earnings
** The Dow Jones industrial average fell 70.73 points, or 1.09 percent, to 6,402.52 after earlier falling nearly 130 points
